new_decisions: | D-151 | **2026-11-03 EST, orchestrator — provisional; the owner may overturn.** AT09 receive-only MTU 1280 TCP rows under D-146: D-146 is the D-137 hardening the owner approved for that row. Such a row may pass on its unchanged byte predicate only when the same run proves the clamp did the work: SYN MSS above 1160 arrives as 1160; every reverse datagram fits 1280 and none is missing; no PTB appears. Without that evidence the row stays blocked under D-137, with measurements retained. UDP and QUIC over a receive-only link stay D-146’s documented limitation. Historical F8-02 rows stay failed. |

| D-152 | **2026-11-03 EST, orchestrator — provisional; the owner may overturn.** Answers isolation 19’s F19-01: judge D-147’s upload negative at production’s applicable destination-deny rule: `ctbadns` for a resolver-only source; `cthost` for a host-only source; `ctdeny` for a denied source and for a source in both denied and host sets. The isolation brief’s literal `ctdeny` meant that applicable rule. No rule order changes. The requirement is unchanged: the member’s upload to the source is dropped, with zero upload usage. |
